```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

```{r load, message = FALSE}
library(nanodRop)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

spectra <- read_nanodrop(system.file("extdata", "nanodrop_example.tsv", package = "nanodRop"))
```

## Absorbance at wavelength pairs

`parse_waves()` pulls out the absorbance at chosen wavelengths for each
measurement and compares them in pairs. With `type = "ratio"` it gives the
usual nucleic acid purity ratios:

```{r ratios}
purity <- parse_waves(spectra, wave_pairs = list(c(260, 280), c(260, 230)), type = "ratio")
head(purity)
```

With the default `type = "diff"` it gives differences, which are useful for
peak heights above a baseline:

```{r diffs}
peaks <- parse_waves(spectra, wave_pairs = list(c(300, 400), c(542, 644)))
head(peaks)
```

Each measurement is its own row, identified by `measurement` (and `file`, if
the data came from `read_nanodrop_dir()`), even when sample names repeat. To
average replicates, group by whatever identifies a sample. In the example file
names like `"6 1"` and `"6 2"` carry the sample and the replicate number:

```{r average}
purity %>%
  mutate(sample = sub(" .*", "", samps)) %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  summarise(across(starts_with("ratio"), mean), replicates = n())
```

## Summaries per spectrum

The output of `read_nanodrop()` is a long table, so dplyr summaries work
directly:

```{r stats}
spectra %>%
  group_by(samps, measurement) %>%
  summarise(
    peak_wavelength = waves[which.max(abs)],
    peak_abs = max(abs),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  head()
```

## Quality checks

```{r qc}
# Measurements with negative absorbance anywhere in the spectrum
spectra %>%
  filter(abs < 0) %>%
  distinct(samps, measurement)

# Every measurement should cover the same wavelengths
spectra %>%
  count(measurement) %>%
  distinct(n)
```

## Smoothing

```{r smoothing, fig.alt = "Original and loess-smoothed absorbance spectra for four samples, one panel per sample."}
smoothed <- spectra %>%
  filter(measurement <= 4) %>%
  group_by(measurement) %>%
  mutate(smoothed = predict(loess(abs ~ waves, span = 0.1))) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(smoothed, aes(waves)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = abs, colour = "Original")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = smoothed, colour = "Smoothed")) +
  facet_wrap(~samps) +
  labs(x = "Wavelength (nm)", y = "Absorbance", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Heatmap

```{r heatmap, fig.alt = "Heatmap of absorbance for each sample across wavelengths."}
ggplot(spectra, aes(waves, factor(measurement), fill = abs)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(x = "Wavelength (nm)", y = "Measurement", fill = "Absorbance") +
  theme_minimal()
```
